text:
**For most full-size fridges, aim for about 1,500-2,000 Wh of battery and an inverter with at least 1,300 W of surge, if you want to cover a full day.** A 1,000 Wh unit gets you roughly 12-17 hours.

**What to check**
- **Running watts:** A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250 W, which almost any 1,000 W-class station can handle ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **Startup surge:** The compressor spikes to about 1,000-2,400 W for a split second. The surge rating is the spec that most often blocks a fridge, so look for at least 1,300 W ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator), [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **Pure sine wave:** Choose this over modified sine wave, which can make compressors run hot or fail to start.
- **Battery capacity:** The compressor only runs about a third of the time, so a typical fridge uses roughly 1,000 Wh per day. With inverter losses and headroom, plan on about 1,400 Wh per day ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Your fridge's yellow EnergyGuide label gives a better number: kWh per year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = average watts. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can use about twice the typical figure.

**Rough guide**
- **~1,000 Wh:** about 12-17 hours.
- **~2,000 Wh:** about 33 hours, so a full day with margin.
- **3,000+ Wh:** 2 or more days, or room for other essentials.

These runtimes assume the door stays closed. HomeGridHQ's estimates use 85% inverter efficiency and a 35% duty cycle ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

**Options from the results**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~1,070 Wh):** about 17 hours, listed around $499. It suits a short outage ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- **Anker SOLIX S2000 (2,010 Wh):** 1,500 W continuous and 3,000 W peak, pure sine wave, about $700 after coupon ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)).
- **BLUETTI AC200L (2,048 Wh):** 2,400 W output, about 33 hours of fridge runtime, expandable to 8,192 Wh. It's $899 at BLUETTI's store, and the Dealectric page says code AFF5OFF takes $44.95 off. [Buy the AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) (affiliate link, and the store's checkout has the final word on price).

I didn't get direct purchase links for the Jackery or Anker units, so use the guide pages above to find current listings.

**Food safety:** The USDA says food becomes unsafe after about 4 hours above 40°F with the door closed, so even a small station that keeps the fridge cycling helps ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

If you tell me your fridge's size or its EnergyGuide kWh/year, and how many hours of outage you want covered, I can narrow this to one pick.
